sources: Cornell Lab of Ornithology (Project FeederWatch, Christmas Bird Count, bird-friendly practices)
note: One tip per month. The tip for today's month is shown on Home.

tips.text: Fresh water is hard to find when everything freezes. Refill a shallow dish with lukewarm water each morning.
Leave seed heads and berries standing. They are winter food, and cutting them back can wait.
Wait to clean up leaves and stems until daytime highs stay around 50 degrees. Insects are still sleeping in them.
Spring is a good time to plant a native shrub. Its roots settle in before the summer heat.
Many birds are nesting in shrubs and hedges right now. Hold off on heavy trimming until late summer.
A fledgling hopping on the ground is usually fine. Its parents are close by. Keep pets away and leave it alone.
In hot weather, refresh the birdbath daily so the water stays cool and clean.
Let coneflowers and black-eyed Susans go to seed. Goldfinches nest late and feed on them.
Fall migration is underway. Turn off extra outdoor lights at night, and mark large windows.
Leave this fall's leaves under your shrubs. Insects shelter there, and birds feed on them in spring. Free.
Cool weather is a good time to plant trees and shrubs. A brush pile gives small birds cover this winter.
Count the birds in your yard. Project FeederWatch and the Christmas Bird Count both welcome backyard watchers.
